637:
(a) Approval required. All entrances and/or exits of any street or drive from or to any public street shall be approved by the city manager or the city manager's designated representative prior to the construction of the street or drive or to the issuance of any building permit for any improvement to be served by such street or drive.
(b) Items to be considered in approval or disapproval. The following items shall be considered in approving or disapproving entrances and exits to public streets:
(1) The width of proposed entrance or exit. Unless approved by the city manager, the maximum width of curb cuts, not including flares or returns at the throat of the facility, for entrances, exits, service drives and similar facilities shall be as follows:
a. Commercial and industrial developments, including offices, retail establishments, banks, restaurants, warehouses, manufacturing and similar developments, 40 feet.
b. Attached single-family residences, multiple-family residential and institutional developments, including apartment buildings, churches, schools, colleges, hospitals and similar developments, 24 feet for two-way entrances and 12 feet for one-way entrances.
c. Single- and two-family residences and townhouses, 12 feet.
(2) The distance of proposed entrance or exit to an existing intersection, to any property line, and/or to any existing or proposed entrance or exit to any existing or proposed street or drive. Except for a single-family residence, two-family residence or townhouse residence, entrances and exits shall be a minimum of 50 feet from the right-of-way line of any existing or proposed intersection, 40 feet from any existing or proposed curb cut, and 20 feet from any existing or proposed property line, unless approved by the city manager.
(3) The number of proposed entrances and exits.
(4) The suitability of the proposed entrance and exit in view of the use and development of adjacent and nearby property.
(5) The suitability of the proposed entrance and exit in view of the amount of traffic on adjacent and nearby streets and the amount of traffic expected from the proposed development.
(6) The suitability of the proposed entrance and exit in view of the impact on the public health, safety and welfare of the community.
(c) Appeals. All persons denied an entrance or exit to a public street by decision of the city manager shall have the right to appeal such decision to the city commission. Such appeal shall be made within 15 days of the date of notice of such decision, shall be in writing, shall state the location of the subject property, the date of the decision being appealed and the reasons upon which the appeal is made.

648:
(a) Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms shall have the following meanings:
Person: Any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Publication vending device: Any self-service or coin-operated box, container, storage unit or other dispenser installed, used or maintained for the display, distribution or sale of publications, newspapers, periodicals, magazines or similar items.
Street: All that area dedicated to public use for public transportation purposes and shall include, but not be limited to, roadways, alleys and sidewalks.
Roadway: That portion of a street improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel.
Public sidewalk: Any surface provided for the use of pedestrians, on any public right-of-way under the jurisdiction of the city.
Publication vending device area: An area of the public sidewalk or other public right-of-way that has been determined by the city commission to be a suitable location for the installation and maintenance of publication vending devices.
(b) Blocking of roadway; placement on sidewalks.
(1) No person shall install, place or maintain any publication vending device which projects onto, into or over any part of the roadway of any public street, or which rests, wholly or in part, upon, along or over any portion of the roadway of any public street.
(2) No person shall install, place or maintain any publication vending device which in whole or in part rests upon, in, or over any public sidewalk, when such installation, use or maintenance endangers the safety of persons or property; or, when such site or location is used for public utility purposes, public transportation purposes or public safety purposes; or, when such publication vending device unreasonably interferes with or impedes the flow of pedestrian or vehicular traffic, including any legally parked or stopped vehicle or the ingress into or egress from any residence or place of business.
(3) No person shall install, place or maintain any publication vending device outside of the assigned publication vending device area.
(c) Permit.
(1) No person shall install, place or maintain any publication vending device which in whole or in part rests upon, in or over any public sidewalk without first obtaining a permit from the city manager or the city manager's designee.
(2) An administrative fee shall be required for the issuance of a publication vending device permit in an amount set by the city manager.
(3) Applications for all permits shall be in writing and must contain the following information:
a. The name, address and telephone number of the applicant to include the address at which the applicant will receive notices as provided through the United States Postal Service and the telephone number to which any notice of repairs or complaints can be directed; and
b. The total number of, and exact location of, each publication vending device to be installed or maintained in the city by the applicant; and
c. An indemnification and hold harmless agreement.
(4) Only one permit shall be required for the placement of any number of publication vending devices by one person, to the extent each location has been listed on the permit application submitted by such person.
(5) Each person is allowed to maintain a maximum of three publication vending device locations.
(6) A permit is valid for one year from date of issue.
(7) A permit shall be granted if the application contains the required information and if the requested installation does not violate the prohibitions set forth in section (b) above and in section (d) below.
(8) Denial of a permit shall be provided in writing listing the reason or reasons for denial.
(9) The applicant shall be given notice of the opportunity to appeal the denial of a permit in writing to the city manager or the city manager's designee. The written appeal must include specific information as to why the permit should not be denied and must be filed within 30 days of the date of the notice of the denial of the permit. In considering an appeal, the city manager or the city manager's designee will apply the standards as described in section (b) above and in section (d) below.
(d) Standards for installation, maintenance and operation. Any permitted publication vending device which in whole or in part rests upon, in or over any public sidewalk shall comply with the following standards:
(1) Any person granted a publication vending device permit shall have said person's name, address, telephone number, and permit number affixed to each publication vending device in a place where such information may be easily located and recognized.
(2) No publication vending device shall exceed 42 inches in height, 30 inches in width and 24 inches in depth. All publication vending devices shall provide for an enclosed, secure and weatherproof area for the storage of publications, newspapers, periodicals, magazines or similar items during the time they are provided for display, distribution or sale. The publication vending device must be on the approved list of publication vending devices maintained in the city manager's office.
(3) Publication vending devices shall be placed adjacent to the wall of a building, parallel to such wall and not more than six inches from the wall.
(4) No publication vending device shall be chained, bolted or otherwise attached to any property without the permission of the owner or person in possession of the property.
(5) No publication vending device shall be chained, bolted or otherwise attached to any city property, including, but not limited to, the sidewalk, trees, benches, light poles, bicycle racks, or trash receptacles.
(6) No publication vending device shall be placed, installed, used or maintained outside an assigned publication vending device area.
(7) Each publication vending device shall be maintained in a clean, neat and attractive condition and in good repair at all times.
(e) Removal of publication vending device.
(1) The city shall cause to be removed any publication vending device on any street or sidewalk in a location in violation of this section. Any publication vending device causing a traffic hazard or other hazard or illegally placed shall be removed at once, with notice given to the owner as soon as practical thereafter. The owner of any such publication vending device shall be assessed the costs for removing the rack as well as any storage costs. The costs shall be satisfied before the publication vending device is released to the owner. The city shall not retain such publication vending devices for more than 30 calendar days.
(2) If a publication vending device is found in a state of disrepair the city will notify the owner via certified United States mail and notice on the machine that the device must be repaired within ten days of notification.
(3) Any publication vending device which has been in disuse for at least 30 days shall be considered abandoned and will be subject to removal as described in subsection (e) above.

(a) Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms shall have the following meanings:
Operation area: The amount of area needed to operate a particular mobile food facility, including both the amount of area occupied by the mobile food facility and an amount of area adjacent to the mobile food facility reasonably sufficient for an individual to operate the mobile food facility.
Person: Any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, or other group or combination acting as a unit, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Mobile food facility: A non-motorized, non-self-propelled vehicle that is readily movable or towable and that is commercially-designed to handle food preparation and service from which food or beverage is sold or offered for sale directly to a consumer.
Street: All that area dedicated to public use for public transportation purposes and shall include, but not be limited to, roadways, alleys and sidewalks.
Roadway: That portion of a street improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel.
Public sidewalk: Any surface provided for the use of pedestrians, on any public right-of-way under the jurisdiction of the city.
(b) Blocking of roadway; placement on sidewalks.
(1) No person shall operate, place or maintain any mobile food facility which projects onto, into or over any part of the roadway of any public street, or which rests, wholly or in part, upon, or over any portion of the roadway of any public street.
(2) No person shall operate, place or maintain a mobile food facility within a public sidewalk, in whole or in part, in a manner that endangers the safety of persons or property or that unreasonably interferes with or impedes the flow of pedestrian or vehicular traffic, including any legally parked or stopped vehicle or the ingress into or egress from any residence or place of business.
(3) No person shall place a mobile food facility that reduces the clear zone of a public sidewalk to a width of less than five feet.
(c) Permit.
(1) No person shall operate, place or maintain any mobile food facility upon, in, within or over any public sidewalk or private property without first obtaining a permit from the city manager or the city manager's designee.
(2) An administrative fee shall be required for the issuance of a mobile food facility permit in an amount set by the city commission.
(3) Applications for all permits shall be in writing and must contain the following information:
a. The name, address and telephone number of the applicant to include the address at which the applicant will receive notices as provided through the United States Postal Service and the telephone number to which any notice of complaints can be directed; and
b. The dimensional height, width and length of the mobile food facility, and the location where the applicant proposes to operate the mobile food facility; and
c. An indemnification and hold harmless agreement (sidewalk permits only); and
d. An affidavit attesting that the applicant either has applied for or will immediately apply for the applicable permit for the operation of the mobile food facility from the DeKalb County Board of Health in accordance with its rules and regulations and certify that the proposed mobile food facility will meet and be operated in conformance with all applicable state laws and regulations, including the Georgia Department of Agriculture, county ordinances and regulations, and city codes and regulations.
(4) If the city manager or their designee determines that an application to operate a mobile food facility is in compliance with the applicable requirements, the city manager or their designee shall approve the application for a permit, but the permit for operation shall not be issued until the applicant has obtained the applicable permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health.
(5) Each person is allowed to operate a maximum of one mobile food facility in the city.
(6) A permit is valid for one year from date of issue.
(7) A permit shall be granted if the application contains the required information and if the requested operation does not violate the prohibitions set forth in section (b) above and in section (d) below.
(8) Denial of a permit shall be provided in writing listing the reason or reasons for denial.
(9) The applicant shall be given notice of the opportunity to appeal the denial of a permit in writing to the city manager or the city manager's designee. The written appeal must include specific information as to why the permit should not be denied and must be filed within 15 days of the date of the notice of the denial of the permit. In considering an appeal, the city manager or his/her designee will apply the standards as described in section (b) above and in section (d) below.
(10) No permit for the operation a mobile food facility shall be transferable.
(11) Permits may be revoked by the city commission for failure of the permittee to comply with the provisions of this section.
(d) Standards for operation. Any permitted mobile food facility shall comply with the following standards:
(1) Any person granted a mobile food facility permit shall have said person's name, address, telephone number, valid city permit, and valid permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health affixed to the mobile food facility in a place where such information is easily visible to the customer.
(2) A mobile food facility shall not exceed a maximum operation area of 36 square feet.
(3) No such mobile food facility shall be operated, placed or maintained within ten feet of any other mobile food facility, said distance to be measured in a straight line from the closet boundary of the operating area of a neighboring facility.
(4) No mobile food facility shall be operated, placed or maintained within 50 feet of any primary entrance of any restaurant within the city.
(5) No mobile food facility shall be operated, place or maintained within 20 feet of the intersection of the right-of-way lines extended of two streets or of a street intersection with a railroad right-of-way line.
(6) No sale or serving of alcohol.
(7) No sale to persons in vehicles.
(8) No amplified sound or loudspeakers.
(9) No lighting, except localized lighting that is used on or in the mobile food facility for the purpose of operating the mobile food facility.
(10) Each mobile food facility shall be maintained in a clean, neat and attractive condition and in good repair at all times.
(11) The on-site presence of an individual owner or employee during hours of operation is required.
(e) Removal of mobile food facility.
(1) The city shall cause to be removed any mobile food facility on any street or sidewalk in a location in violation of this section. Any mobile food facility causing a traffic hazard or other hazard or illegally placed shall be removed at once, with notice given to the owner as soon as practical thereafter. The owner of any such mobile food facility shall be assessed the costs for removal as well as any storage costs. The costs shall be satisfied before the mobile food facility is released to the owner. The city shall not retain such mobile food facility for more than 30 calendar days.
(f) Hours of operation. Mobile food facilities shall only be operated, including sales, set up, take down, and removal, between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday, between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Fridays and Saturdays, and between 9:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. Sundays.

669:
All surface parking lots within commercial C-2 zoning districts, with a total of 30 or more parking spaces, whether primary or accessory in use and whether commercial or noncommercial, shall have minimum barrier curb and landscaping requirements as follows:
(1) Barrier curbs shall be installed around the perimeter of the parking lot and around landscaped areas that are required herein, except where the perimeter abuts an adjacent building or structure and at points of ingress and egress into the facility, so as to prevent encroachment of vehicles onto adjacent property, rights-of-way and landscaped areas.
(2) Barrier curbs shall be a minimum of six inches in height and a minimum of eight inches in width and permanent in nature. Barrier curbs shall be concrete or stone. Such curbs shall be securely installed and maintained in good condition.
(3) Where the end of a parking space abuts a landscaped area, barrier curbs may be placed in the parking space at a maximum of two feet from the end of the parking space. This two-foot-wide area may have the pavement removed and be developed as part of the required landscaped area.
(4) Surface parking lots shall have a minimum landscaped area equal to at least ten percent of the paved area within such lot. In no case shall a parking lot owner be required to provide landscaped areas that exceed ten percent of the paved area.
(5) A minimum of one tree per eight parking spaces shall be included in the required landscaped areas. For the purpose of satisfying this requirement, existing trees that are two and one-half inches or more in caliper as measured at a height of 36 inches above ground level shall be considered to be equivalent to one or more newly planted trees on the basis of one tree for each two and one-half inches of caliper.
(6) In addition to trees, ground cover shall also be provided in order to protect tree roots and to prevent erosion. Ground cover shall consist of shrubs, ivy, liriope, pine bark mulch, and other similar landscaping materials.
(7) Shrubs shall be maintained at a maximum height of two and one-half feet, except where such shrubs are screening the parking surface from an adjacent residential use.
(8) In the event that landscaped areas are in the interior of a parking lot, they shall be a minimum of six feet in length with a minimum area of 36 square feet.
(9) Continuous landscaped buffer strips shall be constructed along sidewalks and public rights-of-way where surface parking lots are adjacent to such sidewalks or public rights-of-way except at points of ingress and egress into the facility. Such landscaped buffer strips shall be a minimum of five feet in width and shall contain, in addition to ground cover, trees planted a maximum of 42½ feet on center along the entire length.
(10) Newly planted trees shall be a minimum of two and one-half inches in caliper as measured at a height of six inches above ground level, shall be a minimum of ten feet in height, shall have a 40-foot minimum mature height, and shall be drought tolerant. Trees shall be planted at a minimum of 30 inches from any barrier curb, so as to prevent injury to trees from vehicle bumpers.
(11) Where landscaped areas are located adjacent to vehicle overhangs, the trees shall be planted in line with the side stripes between parking spaces in order to avoid injury to trees by vehicle bumpers.
(12) All landscaped areas, including trees located in the public right-of-way that are counted in the fulfillment of this requirement, shall be properly maintained in accordance with approved landscape plans. In the event that a tree or any plant material dies, it shall be replaced within six months so as to meet all requirements of this section and to allow for planting in the appropriate planting season.
(13) If it is determined by the city arborist that implementation of these regulations will result in the loss of parking spaces in existing lots, the public works director may increase the allowable percentage compact car spaces from 25 percent up to 35 percent so as to minimize the loss of parking spaces.
(14) Notwithstanding subsection (13) above, existing parking lots shall not be required to reduce the number of parking spaces by more than three percent as a result of implementing these landscaping regulations.
(15) Upon written application by any person subject to the provisions of this section, the city manager and/or the city manager's designee is hereby authorized to grant administrative variances to the requirements of this section only upon making all of the following findings:
a. There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property in question because of its size, shape, topography, subsurface conditions, overhead structures, or the existence of sufficient trees in the public right-of-way within ten feet of the property line;
b. Such conditions are peculiar to the particular piece of property involved; and
c. Relief, if granted, would not cause substantial detriment to the public good or impair the purposes and intent of this article.

The applicant shall notify the city manager in writing, by person or by mail, of the appeal within three days of filing an appeal with the municipal court.
(c) The municipal court judge shall hear the appeal at the next available court session. The judge shall hear evidence as to the reasons the application was denied by the director of public safety and the city manager. The judge shall approve, disapprove, or amend the application. The decision of the municipal court judge is final.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
682:
The director of public safety or a designated representative, in denying an application for a special event permit, may authorize the conduct of the special event on a date, a time, or over a route different from that named by the applicant. An applicant desiring to accept an alternate permit shall within two days after notice of the action file a written notice of acceptance with the office of the director of public safety. An alternate permit shall conform to the requirements of, and shall have the effect of, a special event permit under this article.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
685:
(a) A permittee shall comply with all permit directions and conditions and with all applicable local, state and federal laws and ordinances.
(b) The special event leader shall carry the special event permit upon the special event leader's person during the conduct of the special event.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96; Ord. No. O-22-11, § 2(Exh. A), 10-17-22)
686:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to hamper, obstruct, impede or interfere with any special event or with any person, animal or vehicle participating or used in a special event.
(b) The director of public safety or a designated representative shall have the authority to prohibit or restrict the parking of vehicles along a roadway constituting a part of the route of a special event. When necessary, the police department shall post signs to the effect and it shall be unlawful for any person to park or leave unattended any vehicle in violation thereof. Police officers may cause to be impounded any vehicle unlawfully parked in violation of this article.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
687:
It shall be unlawful for any person to distribute or cause to be distributed from any vehicle participating in a parade or procession in the public streets any item to any spectator or bystander.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
688:
The director of public safety or a designated representative shall have the authority to revoke a special event permit at any time during conduct of the special event in the event of failure to conform to or comply with the standards for issuance as set forth in section 86-156. The director of public safety or a designated representative may at any time revoke a parade permit when, by reason of disaster, public calamity, riot or other emergency, the safety of public or private property requires such revocation.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
689:
(a) The director of public safety is authorized to classify the special event using the following criteria:
(1) The anticipated amount of extra personnel which shall be required to be furnished by the city to accomplish the necessary public safety and sanitation components of the special event. By agreement, as endorsed upon the special event permit, the applicant may furnish some or all of the personnel requirements and the classification shall be considered and reduced accordingly;
(2) The type and amount of special or technical assistance required from city employees;
(3) The anticipated number of spectators and participants over the entire period of the special event, determined in accordance with section 86-155(h); and
(4) Whether the organization(s) producing and/or sponsoring the special event is/are profit-making or nonprofit.
(b) The classes of special event permits shall be as follows:
(1) Class A permit: For a special event which will require between 100-200 extra staff hours by city employees in any department or in which the approximate number of spectators and participants, as determined in accordance with section 86-155(h), is 8,000 or more persons, and is being held by a profit-making organization.
(2) Class B permit: For a special event which has the characteristics of a class A permit but which is organized and executed by a nonprofit organization.
(3) Class C permit: For a special event which will require between 50-99 extra staff hours by city employees in any department or in which the approximate number of spectators and participants, as determined in accordance with section 86-155(h), is between 3,000 and 8,000 persons, and is being held by a profit-making organization.
(4) Class D permit: For a special event which has the characteristics of a class C permit but which is organized and executed by a nonprofit organization.
(5) Class E permit: For a special event which will require less than 50 extra staff hours by city employees in any department or in which the approximate number of spectators and participants, as determined in accordance with section 86-155(h), is 3,000 persons or less and is being held by a profit-making organization.
(6) Class F permit: For a special event which has the characteristics of a class C permit but is organized and executed by a nonprofit organization.
(c) The permit fee and the sanitation bond shall be as follows:
| Permit Fees | Sanitation Bond
Class A permit | $500.00 | $300.00
Class B & C permit | 300.00 | 200.00
Class D & E permit | 100.00 | 100.00
Class F permit | 50.00 | 50.00
Any special event requiring in excess of the agreed upon city staffing hours shall be charged a prorated fee in addition to the initial base fee. Upon satisfactory completion of the sanitation bond agreement, the sanitation bond shall be refunded to the applicant.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
690:
Prior to the issuance of a special event permit, the permit applicant or a duly authorized officer of the sponsoring organization must sign an agreement to reimburse the city for any costs incurred in repairing damage to city property resulting from or in connection with a permitted event. The agreement shall also provide that the permittee or sponsoring organization shall defend the city against, and indemnify and hold the city harmless from, any liability to or claims of liability by any persons resulting from any alleged damage or injury occurring in connection with the special event.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
691:
The applicant or sponsoring organization must possess or obtain public liability insurance to protect against loss from liability imposed by law for damages on account of bodily injury and property damage arising from the special event. The insurance shall name on the policy as additional insured the city, its officers, employees and agents. Insurance coverage must be maintained for the duration of the event. A copy of the policy or a certificate of insurance along with all necessary endorsements must be filed with the city manager's office no later than seven days before the date of the special event. The minimum limit of insurance is $500,000.00.
(Ord. No. O-96-10, 7-8-96)
692:
Footnote 3:
Editor's note— Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, adopted Dec. 2, 2019, amended Art. VII in its entirety to read as herein set out. Former X, §§ 86-170—86-198, pertained to the same subject matter, and derived from Ord. No. O-17-03, § 1, adopted March 29, 2017.
693:
The city is vitally concerned with the use, construction within, and occupancy of all rights-of-way in the city as such rights-of-way are a valuable and limited resource which must be utilized to promote the public health, safety, welfare, and economic development of the city and to protect public work infrastructure. Therefore, the city, under the authority of the laws and Constitution of the State of Georgia, has adopted this article for the purpose of regulating public and private entities which use the city rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
694:
The provisions of this article shall apply to all utilities and facilities occupying the rights-of-way as provided herein.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
696:
Each utility that occupies, uses or has facilities in the rights-of-way at the time of passage of this article, including by lease, sublease or assignment, to operate facilities located in the rights-of-way, unless specifically exempted by state or federal law or this Code, shall file a registration statement with the city manager within 90 days of the effective date of this article.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
697:
The registration information provided to the city shall be on a form approved by the city manager, which shall include, but not be limited to:
1. The name, legal status (i.e. partnership, corporation, etc.), street address, email address, and telephone and facsimile numbers of the utility filing the registration statement (the "registrant"). If the registrant is not the owner of the facility in the rights-of-way, the registration shall include the name, street address, email address if applicable, and telephone and facsimile numbers of the owner;
2. The name, street address, email address and telephone and facsimile numbers of one or more facilities representative(s). Current information regarding how to contact the facilities representative(s), in an emergency shall be provided at the time of filing a registration and shall be updated as necessary to assure accurate contact information is available to the city at all times;
3. A copy of the utility's certificate of authority (or other acceptable evidence of authority to operate) from the Georgia Public Service Commission and/or the FCC and any other similar approvals, permits, or agreements.
4. A copy of the service agreement, if applicable or other legal instrument that authorizes the utility to use or occupy the rights-of-way for the purpose described in the registration.
5. A copy of the approved annual work plan required by Section 9.1.8 of Part IV of this Code.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
698:
If a registration is incomplete, the city manager shall notify the registrant and require that the registration be completed within 14 days of registrant's receipt of such notice. If a registration is complete, the city manager shall so notify the registrant in writing.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
699:
Acceptance of the registration shall not convey title in the rights-of-way. Acceptance of the registration is only the nonexclusive, limited right to occupy rights-of-way in the city for the limited purposes stated in the acceptance. Acceptance of the registration does not excuse a utility from obtaining permits required by city ordinances nor from obtaining appropriate access or pole attachment agreements before using the facilities of others, including the city. Acceptance of the registration does not excuse a utility from notifying the city of construction as required herein, nor does such acceptance relieve any responsibility for compliance with franchises previously granted by the city or with franchise requirements in Chapter 96 of Part III of this Code.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
700:
Beginning one year after the effective date of this article, any facilities or part of a facility found in a rights-of-way for which registration is required but has not been obtained unless specifically exempted by law, and/or for which no valid service agreement exists with the city, may be deemed to be a nuisance and an unauthorized use of the rights-of-way. The city may exercise any remedies or rights it has at law or in equity, including, but not limited to: abating the nuisance; taking possession of the facilities; evicting the utility from the rights-of-way; prosecuting the violator and/or any other remedy provided by city ordinance.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
701:
It shall be unlawful for any utility to excavate or to construct, install, maintain, renew, remove or relocate facilities in, on, along, over or under the rights-of-way of the city without a utility permit from the city manager in accordance with the terms of this article.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
702:
Utility permits shall be obtained from the city manager upon application made on forms prescribed by the city manager. The written application shall be accompanied by the following:
1. An indemnity bond or other acceptable security in an amount to be set by the city to pay for any damages to any part of the city road system or other public or private property or to any city employee or member of the public caused by activity or work of the utility performed under authority of the permit issued;
2. A copy, if requested, of the registrant's certificate of authority (or other acceptable evidence of authority to operate) from the Georgia Public Service Commission and/or the FCC and any other similar approvals, permits, or agreements; and
3. A copy, if requested, of the service agreement, if applicable, or other legal instrument that authorizes the utility to use or occupy the rights-of-way for the purpose described in the application.
4. The applicable permit fee.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
703:
Fees shall be established by the city commission and set forth in the schedule of fees.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
704:
If the city manager determines the applicant has satisfied the following requirements, the city manager may issue a utility permit:
1. Whether issuing of the approval will be consistent with this article; and
2. Whether applicant has submitted a complete application and has secured all certificates and other authorizations required by law, if applicable, in order to construct facilities in the manner proposed by the applicant; and
3. Whether the application provides sufficient mitigation of impact on safety, visual quality of the streets, traffic flow, and other users of the rights-of-way and the difficulty and expected length of project construction or maintenance; and
4. Whether the application includes adequate provisions for general public notice and direct notification to parties that will be impacted by issuance of the permit.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
705:
(a) Each utility shall, as soon as reasonably practicable, notify the city manager of any event regarding its facilities which it considers to be an emergency. The utility may proceed to take whatever actions are necessary in order to respond to the emergency. A utility that engages in an emergency excavation shall take all reasonable precautions to avoid or minimize damage to any existing facilities and structures.
(b) In the event that the city becomes aware of an emergency regarding utility facilities, the city may attempt to contact the affected utility, through its facilities representative(s). The city may take whatever action it deems necessary in order to respond to the emergency, including cutting or moving any of the wires, cables, amplifiers, appliances, or other parts of the facilities. The city shall not incur any liability to the utility for such emergency actions and the reasonable cost of such work shall be paid by each utility affected by the emergency.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
706:
(a) Each utility permit shall have set commencement and expiration dates based on information provided in the applicant's permit application.
(b) The utility permit shall remain in place until construction is completed or until its expiration date unless the utility is in default. The city manager may give written notice of default to a utility if it is determined that a utility has:
(1) Violated any provision or requirement of the issuance or acceptance of a utility permit application or any law of the city, state, or federal government;
(2) Attempted to evade any provision or requirement of this article;
(3) Engaged in any fraud or deceit upon the city; or
(4) Made a material misrepresentation or omission of fact in its permit application.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
707:
If a utility fails to cure a default within 20 days of receipt of such notice provided to the utility by the city, then such default shall be a material breach and city may terminate the utility permit.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
708:
If work is not begun within six months of the date of issuance, the utility permit will automatically expire.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
709:
The latest edition of the utility accommodation policy and standards manual, including all references contained therein to codes, rules, regulations, schedules, forms and appendix items, except Appendix B (permit forms and supporting documents), promulgated by the State of Georgia Department of Transportation, as may be amended from time to time, and the city's administrative standards are hereby adopted by reference and incorporated in this article as if fully set forth herein, subject to the amendments and modification contained in this article. Copies of the manual and administrative standards shall be maintained by the city manager and available for public inspection. Any conflicts between the provisions of this article, the manual, and the administrative standards shall be resolved in the following order of superiority: administrative standards; followed by manual; followed by this article. References to state personnel, agencies, and fees shall be interpreted, where required, as meaning the City of Decatur municipal equivalents.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
710:
Unless specifically provided in the permit, no utility may occupy the city rights-of-way unless:
1. Sufficient space is available so that the free flow and safety of traffic and other capacity considerations are not unduly impaired;
2. The installation does not prevent the city from reasonably maintaining the streets, structures, traffic control devices and other appurtenant facilities; and
3. Maintenance and operations of the facilities do not jeopardize the traffic, street structure, other users of the rights-of-way or the rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
711:
In the event the city needs to modify the grades, lines, or improvements for any street within the city's rights-of-way during the term of the utility permit and the modification involves an area in which the utility's facilities are located, the utility shall, at its own cost and expense, protect or promptly alter or relocate the facilities, or any part thereof, so as to conform with such new grades or lines. Unless agreed to by the city, such actions shall be completed within 14 days of receipt of a written request from the city to undertake such actions. In the event the utility refuses or neglects to so protect, alter, or relocate all or part of the facilities, the city shall have the right to break through, remove, alter, or relocate all or any part of the facilities without any liability to the utility and the utility shall pay to the city the costs incurred in connection with such breaking through, removal, alteration, or relocation.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
712:
Unless otherwise expressly provided in a valid service agreement, no placement of any facility of the utility is to be considered a vested interest in the rights-of-way, and such facilities are to be removed, relocated underground, or modified by the utility at its own expense whenever the city determines that the public convenience would be enhanced thereby. The facilities shall be so located and installed as to cause minimum interference with the rights and convenience of property owners in the immediate vicinity of the installation.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
713:
As provided in O.C.G.A § 25-9-6 (the Georgia Utility Facility Protection Act) and other applicable state law currently in place or as amended, no utility shall commence, perform, or engage in blasting or in excavating with mechanized excavating facilities unless and until the utility planning the blasting or excavating has given 48 hours' notice by submitting a locate request to the utility protection center, beginning the next business day after such notice is provided, excluding hours during days other than business days.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
714:
Each utility shall be responsible for the cost of repairing any facilities in the rights-of-way and any adjoining property or other facilities which are damaged by the utility or its facilities.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
715:
A utility shall be liable, at its own cost and expense, to replace, restore or repair, any street, facilities or property or structure thereon, thereunder, thereover or adjacent thereto that may become disturbed or damaged as a result of the construction or installation, operation, upgrade, repair or removal of facilities. such replacement or repair shall return the damaged street, facilities or property or structure to a condition as good as or better than its condition before the work performed by the utility that caused such disturbance or damage. If the utility does not commence such replacement or repair within 20 days after receipt of written notice from the city, the city may make such replacement or repair and the utility shall pay the reasonable and actual cost of the same.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
716:
The utility shall make the construction site available to the city manager and to all others as authorized by law for inspection at all reasonable times during the execution and upon completion of the construction.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
717:
At any time, including the time of inspection, the city manager may order the immediate cessation of any work which poses a serious threat to the health, safety, or welfare of the public, violates any law, or violates the terms and conditions of the utility permit and/or this article or issue an order to correct work which does not conform to the utility permit and/or applicable standards, conditions or codes.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
718:
When the construction under any utility permit is completed, the utility shall notify the city manager.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
719:
The utility shall obtain all construction, building and other permits and approvals required by City Code and by state and federal law. In addition, the holder of a utility permit shall comply with all requirements of laws, shall complete work in a rights-of-way as to not cause any unnecessary or unauthorized obstructions of sidewalks, streets, waterways or railways, and shall be responsible for all work done in the rights-of-ways regardless of who performs the work. No obstruction of or excavation in the rights-of-way may be performed when seasonally prohibited or when conditions are unreasonable for such work, except in the case of an emergency as outlined in section 86-182 of this article. Registration in accordance with this article does not relieve an applicant of responsibility for compliance with Chapter 96 of Part III of this Code.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
720:
Any person guilty of a violation of this article shall be punished, upon conviction, as provided in Section 1-12 of Part III of this Code. In addition to the penalty prescribed above, the city may pursue other remedies such as abatement of nuisances, injunctive relief and revocation of licenses or permits.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
721:
The city, by issuing a written approval of registration under this article, does not surrender or to any extent lose, waive, impair, or lessen the lawful powers and rights, which it has now or may be hereafter vested in the city under the Constitution and Laws of the United States, State of Georgia and the City Charter, and under the provisions of the City Code to regulate the use of the rights-of-way. The utility, by applying for and being issued a written utility permit, is deemed to acknowledge that all lawful powers and rights, regulatory power, or police power, or otherwise as are or the same may be from time to time vested in or reserved to the city, shall be in full force and effect and subject to the exercise thereof by the city at any time. A utility is deemed to acknowledge that its interests are subject to the regulatory and police powers of the city to adopt and enforce general ordinances necessary to the safety and welfare of the public and is deemed to agree to comply with all applicable general laws enacted by the city pursuant to such powers. in particular, all utilities shall comply with city zoning and other land use requirements pertaining to the placement and specifications of facilities.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19)
722:
(a) Small wireless facility standards. Small wireless facilities must be compatible in size, mass, and color to similar facilities in the same zoning area, with a goal of minimizing the physical and visual impact on the area. Facilities must be located in alignment with existing trees and/or facilities. Facilities must maintain the integrity and character of the neighborhoods and corridors in which the facilities are located.
(b) Historic district. Small wireless facilities installed in a local or national historic district shall conform to the provisions of the district(s) architectural guidelines.
(c) Streetscape guidelines. Small wireless facilities shall conform to the streetscape standards as identified in the Unified Development Ordinance as well as the Downtown Decatur Streetscape Guidelines.
(d) Camouflaging. Small wireless facilities must be designed using camouflaging techniques that make them as unobtrusive as possible if (i) it is not possible or desirable to match the design and color of facilities with the similar facilities in the same zoning area or (ii) existing facilities in the area are out of character with a streetscape plan or other aesthetic plan that has been adopted by the city.
(e) Concealment. Small wireless facilities may incorporate specific concealment elements to minimize visual impacts per the direction of the city manager, or the city manager's designee. Concealment elements may include public art, decorative poles, sanitation receptacles, and street furniture, etc.
(f) Installation and modification standards. Installation of new small wireless facilities in, on, along, over, or under the public rights-of-way or modification of existing facilities in, on, along, over, or under the public rights-of-way shall:
(1) Minimize risks to public safety;
(2) Ensure that placement of facilities on existing structures is within the tolerance of those structures;
(3) Ensure that installations and modifications are subject to periodic review to minimize the intrusion on the right-of-way;
(4) Ensure that the city bears no risk or liability as a result of the installations or modifications; and
(5) Ensure that use of the public rights-of-way does not inconvenience the public, interfere with the primary uses of the public rights-of-way, or hinder the ability of the city or other government entities to improve, modify, relocate, abandon, or vacate the right-of-way or any portion thereof, or to cause the improvement, modification, relocation, vacation, or abandonment of small wireless facilities in the right-of-way.
(g) Plans for use. No small wireless facilities shall be placed in, on, along, over, or under the public rights-of-way unless: (i) there are immediate plans to use the proposed facility; or (ii) there is a contract with another party that has immediate plans to use the proposed facility.
(1) At any point in time, the city reserves the right to request verification from the wireless infrastructure provider and/or inspect each facility to ensure current usage of all components. If found vacant or not fully utilized, the city will require removal or use of those portions not in use.
(h) Contact information. Every small wireless facility placed in the public rights-of-way shall at all times display signage that accurately identifies the facility owner and provides the facility owner's unique site number, and also provides a local or toll-free telephone number to contact the facility owner's operations center.
(Ord. No. O-19-18, § 1, 12-2-19; Ord. No. O-22-11, § 2(Exh. A), 10-17-22)

730:
(a) The intent of this article is to levy an excise tax on rooms, lodgings, and accommodations to provide additional funding for the promotion of tourism, conventions, and trade shows in the City of Decatur, Georgia.
(b) The purpose of this article is to enact an excise tax upon the furnishing for value to the public of any room or rooms, lodgings or accommodations furnished by any person or legal entity licensed by or required to pay business or occupational taxes to the City of Decatur, Georgia for operating within the city a hotel, motel, inn, lodge, tourist camp, tourist cabin, rental cabin, short-term rental, or any other place in which rooms, lodgings, or accommodations are regularly furnished for value.
(c) This excise tax shall be imposed under the authorization of Act 532(SB 477) of the 2018 Regular Session of the Georgia General Assembly, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b).
(Ord. No. O-18-13, 7-16-18; Ord. No. O-24-02, § 1.1, 5-20-2024)
732:
There is hereby set and levied on the occupant of a guest room of any hotel/motel/cabin/residence/lodge/short-term rental located within the city a tax in the amount of eight percent of the gross rent for such occupancy.
(Ord. No. O-18-13, 7-16-18; Ord. No. O-24-02, § 3.1, 5-20-2024)
734:
(a) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(b)(5)(A), an amount equal to not less than 50 percent of the total amount of taxes collected that exceed the amount of taxes that would be collected at the rate of five percent shall be expended for promoting tourism, conventions, and trade shows by the destination marketing organization, as defined in this ordinance, designated by the city commission of the City of Decatur, Georgia; and

(Code 1967, § 14-130)
772:

(Code 1967, § 14-131)

(1) Between the front building line and the front property line except on a bona fide paved or graveled driveway leading to a garage, carport or other permanent parking space located to the rear of the front building line.

(a) Definitions.
(1) Bicycle lane means a portion of the roadway that has been designated by striping, pavement, markings, or signage for the exclusive or preferential use of persons operating bicycles.
(b) No person shall drive or otherwise operate a motor vehicle in, on, or across a bicycle lane except:
(1) When turning into or leaving property adjacent to the roadway;
(2) When turning onto or from another public or private roadway;
(3) When turning into or leaving a designated, on-street parking space;
(4) When yielding the right of way to an authorized emergency vehicle; or
(5) When driving an authorized emergency vehicle in the performance of duty.
(c) No person shall park a motor vehicle in, on, or across a bicycle lane except:
(1) When necessary for an authorized emergency vehicle in the performance of duty;
(2) When necessary to do so because the motor vehicle is inoperable, as that term is defined in section 98-5; or
(3) When directed to do so by a police officer.

779:
In order to facilitate traffic control during construction activity, special events, times of emergency, and similar circumstances, the city manager may designate streets or parts of streets where parking on the designated street or part of street is allowed only for such persons who have obtained a permit issued by the city manager. When a street or part of street has been so designated and signs with the legend 'permit parking only' have been erected, it shall be unlawful for any person other than those who have a permit to park a vehicle on said street or part of street. Streets or part of streets may be designated for permit parking only restrictions for a period of no more than 12 months.

782:
Parking meter zones of the city shall be as established by the city commission and, when so established and clearly marked as such, or upon parking meters being installed, such areas shall be the parking meter zones of the city.
(Code 1967, § 14-103)
783:
Parking meters shall be installed under the supervision of the city manager and the chief of police in all parking meter zones. The parking meters shall be placed upon the curb immediately adjacent to the individual parking places. Each parking meter shall be placed or set in such manner as to show or display by a signal that the parking space adjacent to such meter is or is not legally in use. Each parking meter installed shall indicate by a proper legend the legal parking time established by the city, and, when operated, shall indicate on and by its dial and pointer the duration of the period of legal parking, and on the expiration of such period shall indicate "violation," or over parking.
(Code 1967, § 14-104)
784:
The city manager and the chief of police shall have lines or markings painted or placed upon the curb or upon the street adjacent to each parking meter for the purpose of designating the parking space for which the meter is to be used. Each vehicle parking adjacent or next to any parking meter shall park within the lines or markings so established. It shall be unlawful to park any vehicle across any such line or marking or to park any vehicle in such a position that it shall not be entirely within the area so designated by such lines or markings.
(Code 1967, § 14-105)
785:
When a parking space in any parking meter zone is at an angle to the adjacent curb or sidewalk, any vehicle parking in such parking space shall be parked with the front of such vehicle nearest to such meter.
(Code 1967, § 14-106)
786:

Upon the deposit of such coin or coins and the placing of such meter in operation, the parking space may be lawfully occupied by such vehicle during the period of parking time which has been purchased, as indicated on the meter, for the part of the street in which the parking space is located. If such vehicle shall remain parked in any such parking space beyond the parking time limit fixed for such parking space, the parking meter shall, by its dial and pointer, indicate such illegal parking by displaying the word "expired," and, in that event, such vehicle shall be considered as parked overtime and beyond the period of legal parking time.
(Code 1967, § 14-107; Ord. No. O-22-11, § 2(Exh. A), 10-17-22)

(Code 1967, § 14-108)
788:

794:
(a) Business license required. It shall be unlawful for any person, either as principal, agent or employee, to use or operate upon any of the streets of the city a wrecker or to do any trespass towing without having obtained a business license granted pursuant to chapter 22 of this Code.
(b) Removal only in areas properly posted. It shall be unlawful for a person hired by the owner of private property within the city to remove vehicles from any off-street parking facility or to do any trespass towing unless there shall have been previously posted on the property the signs required to be posted as provided by this section and as provided by O.C.G.A. § 44-1-13.
(1) Signs shall be located at each designated entrance to a parking lot or parking area where parking prohibitions are to be effective. Where there is not a designated entrance, such signs shall be erected so as to be clearly visible from each and every parking space.
(2) The wording on such signs shall state that any vehicle parked thereon which is not authorized to be parked in such area may be removed at a maximum cost, as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, and stored at a maximum cost, as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, per day, to be paid by the owner, shall state the address of the location to which such vehicles are towed, shall state that checks and credit cards shall be accepted in lieu of cash and for no additional fee, shall state that no storage fee may be charged if the vehicle has been held less than 24 hours, shall state that these conditions are required by state law and city ordinances, and shall state that complaints may be made to the police division at 373-6551. The lettering on such signs shall be black on a white, reflective grade background, and shall be illuminated if out of headlight range.
(Ord. No. O-91-20, § 1(12½-72), 9-3-91)
795:
The operator of any wrecker service vehicle summoned to tow away any vehicle, whether on a public street, public property or private property, shall not tow the vehicle away and shall not charge any fee if the operator of the vehicle returns prior to the wrecker vehicle having left the location to which it was summoned.
(Ord. No. O-91-20, § 1(12½-73), 9-3-91)
796:
(a) Any towing and storage firm engaged in the business of trespass towing shall not charge the owner of any towed vehicle or personal property in excess of an amount set forth in the schedule of fees and charges for the removal of the vehicle or personal property, or in excess of an amount set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, per day, for storage fees; provided, however, that no storage fees shall be charged for the first 24-hour period from the time the vehicle or personal property is removed from the property. The fee set forth in the schedule of fees and charges shall be all inclusive. No additional fees may be charged for using dollies, trailers, lifts, slim jims, or any other equipment or service. However, the maximum fees in this section shall not apply to the trespass towing of vehicles which weigh in excess of two tons.
(b) Any towing and storage firm engaged in the business of trespass towing shall accept payment of fees in each of the following ways: in cash; by check, if proper identification is provided; and by at least one major credit card.
(c) Trespass towing and storage fees shall be established annually by the city commission after receiving recommendations from the city manager based on financial information submitted by the trespass towing firms as to their costs for the removal and storage of vehicles and personal property and on other information and shall be set forth in the schedule of fees and charges. Information shall be submitted by licensees by October 31 of each year.
(Ord. No. O-91-20, § 1(12½-74), 9-3-91)
797:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person, except for law enforcement personnel, to affix mechanical locking devices, including those commonly referred to as "boots," to any automobile parked in any off-street parking facility, lot or area located on private property within the city, regardless of whether a charge for parking is assessed, unless the following conditions are met:
(1) Signs shall be located at each designated entrance and exit to the parking facility, lot or area where such a device is to be used indicating that parking prohibitions are in effect, such signs being erected so as to be clearly visible upon entering and exiting the lot. Signs shall also be erected within the lot, so that a sign can be clearly visible from each and every parking space. For the purpose of this section, the term "clearly visible" shall mean the sign is posted facing the restricted parking spaces, the sign is positioned so that the bottom edge is at least four feet from the ground and no more than six feet from the ground and at least one sign is posted for every row of parking spaces. Any row of parking spaces in excess of 30 feet shall have one sign posted every 30 feet.
(2) Signs shall be a minimum of 30 inches by 30 inches in size and lettering on the sign shall be a minimum of ¾ inch in height.
(3) The wording on such signs shall contain the following information:
a. A statement that any vehicle parked thereon which is not authorized to be parked in such area may be subject to use of a mechanical locking device.
b. Set forth the maximum fee for removal of the device.
c. The name, address and phone number of the company setting the device.
d. The name, address and phone number of the owner of the parking facility, lot or area.
e. A statement that cash and credit cards are accepted for payment.
f. A statement that no additional fee will be charged for use of credit cards.
g. Reserved.
h. A statement that if you leave the lot you will be booted.
i. A statement that lists the names of the businesses served by the parking lot.
(4) Phone numbers referenced in subsection (2)c. above must be operable and answered in person during the hours mechanical locking devices are in use.
(5) Lettering on such signs shall be black on white. If mechanical locking devices are to be utilized before 7:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m., the signs shall have a reflective grade background, and be illuminated if out of headlight range.
(6) The operator of the mechanical locking device shall remain on-site at the parking facility, lot or area at all times when mechanical locking devices are in use and affixed to a vehicle. The attendant shall have immediate access to equipment to remove or release the locking device. The attendant shall have the means to accept and receive payment in cash, or by at least one major credit card.
(7) The operator of the mechanical locking device must wear an identification badge listing the name and address of the company employing the operator, the operator's first name, and a passport sized photo of the operator.
(8) Equipment used to collect payment for use of the parking facility, lot or area must have been able to accept both cash and credit card payments at all times within the preceding 12 hour period.
(9) No fee shall be assessed for the removal of a mechanical locking device in excess of $75.00 per day.
(b) Parking facilities, lots or areas that assess a charge for use of the facility, lot or area can use mechanical locking devices only when a paper or electronic receipt for each paid parking charge is provided at the time of payment. The receipt shall include the address of the lot and the time and date of payment.
(c) Parking facilities, lots or areas that assess a charge for the use of the facility, lot or area, must provide parking payment options that include both cash and credit card options.

Police officers may cause to be impounded:
(1) A motor vehicle unlawfully parked in violation of a provision of this Code or any state law which prohibits the parking of vehicles at the place where or the time when the impounded motor vehicle is found.
(2) A motor vehicle, the continued presence of which, because of the physical location or condition of the motor vehicle, poses a danger to the public safety or to the motor vehicle.
(3) A motor vehicle from which the driver has been arrested for a violation of traffic laws or any other offense and there is no other alternative driver or custodian for the motor vehicle immediately available.
(4) A motor vehicle which is a stolen vehicle or is subject to seizure and forfeiture under the laws of the state or is subject to being held for use as evidence in a criminal trial.
(Ord. No. O-91-02, § 14-149, 3-4-91)
801:
In all cases where the owner or operator of a motor vehicle which is on a public street has requested that the motor vehicle be left unattended at that location in lieu of the impoundment of the motor vehicle pursuant to section 98-111(1) and (3), the police officer may, in the police officer's discretion, honor the request for a period of time not exceeding 24 hours, after which time the motor vehicle shall be impounded if not removed by the owner or operator. Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the authority of a police officer to impound a vehicle pursuant to section 98-111(2) and (4).
(Ord. No. O-91-02, § 14-150, 3-4-91)
802:
(a) When a police officer intends to impound a motor vehicle and the owner or operator of the motor vehicle is then present, except if the impoundment is being made pursuant to section 98-111(4), the police officer shall, before the motor vehicle is removed, provide the owner or operator with a notice that the motor vehicle is being impounded, that towing and storage charges will be assessed against the impounded motor vehicle, that the owner may claim and regain possession of the impounded motor vehicle at the location to which it is being removed for storage without prepayment of towing and storage charges upon posting with the custodian of the vehicle a cash bond in the amount of the accrued towing and storage charges, and that the owner may request a hearing as to the propriety of the impoundment and as to the amount of and the owner's liability for the towing and storage charges. The notice shall also state the location where the impounded motor vehicle will be stored and the place where the owner may make the request for the hearing. The notice shall also state that failure by the owner to request a hearing within five days of receipt of the notice may act as a waiver of the right to a hearing and that this may result in the placing of a lien against the motor vehicle for the towing and storage charges without further notice to the owner. The owner of the impounded vehicle shall sign the notice as an acknowledgment that a copy has been received, and a copy of the notice shall be provided to the owner.
(b) When a police officer impounds and removes a motor vehicle pursuant to section 98-111(1) or (2) and the owner or the person with the right of possession of the motor vehicle is not present at the time of the impoundment, notice containing the same language as required in subsection (a) of this section shall be served, within five days from the date of impoundment, upon the owner by posting such notice in the United States mail with sufficient postage to ensure its delivery to the address shown for the owner in the motor vehicle registration records of the state in which the motor vehicle is registered.
(c) If a person required by this section to sign a notice of impoundment willfully fails or refuses to do so, the police officer shall note this fact on the face of the notice which shall constitute prima facie evidence of delivery or service of notice as required by this section.
(Ord. No. O-91-02, § 14-151, 3-4-91)
803:
(a) Unless the motor vehicle is impounded pursuant to section 98-111(4), the owner of an impounded motor vehicle may secure the release of the motor vehicle from impoundment upon requesting the release and presenting proof of ownership satisfactory to the clerk of the city municipal court. If the clerk of court is satisfied that the person making the request is the owner or authorized agent of the owner, the clerk of court shall provide a release to the owner or authorized agent, and, upon the presenting of this release and the payment of accrued towing and storage charges to the custodian of the motor vehicle, the custodian shall release the motor vehicle.
(b) If the owner of the motor vehicle requests a hearing, such request shall be made to the clerk of court of the municipal court and the clerk of court shall schedule the hearing in the municipal court. The clerk of court shall then provide the release, as specified in subsection (a) of this section, and, upon the presenting of this release and the posting of a cash bond in the amount of the accrued towing and storage charges with the custodian of the motor vehicle, the custodian shall release the vehicle.
(Ord. No. O-91-02, § 14-152, 3-4-91)
804:
(a) If the owner of an impounded motor vehicle or the owner's agent timely requests a hearing on the impoundment and the charges, such hearing shall be before a judge in the city's municipal court.
(b) At the hearing, the owner, the owner's agent or attorney shall be afforded an opportunity to present, by oral testimony or documentary evidence, objections to:
(1) The impoundment of the motor vehicle.
(2) The amount of the towing and storage charges or the owner's liability for the payment thereof.
(c) If the owner or the owner's agent requests the hearing more than five days after the owner received a copy of the notice of impoundment, the owner, the owner's agent or attorney shall be required at the hearing, as a condition precedent to the presentation of any objections by the owner, to show good cause for the delay in making the request. If good cause cannot be shown, the judge shall dismiss the hearing and make the finding stated in subsection (d)(2) of this section; otherwise, the judge shall proceed to hear the owner's objections.
(d) At the conclusion of the hearing on the owner's objections, the judge shall render a decision.
(1) If the judge finds that the impoundment was improper, the judge shall:
a. Find that the owner is not liable for a towing or storage charge occasioned by the impoundment; and
b. Determine whether and to what extent the city shall bear the expense of the towing and storage charges.
(2) If the judge finds that the impoundment was proper, the judge shall establish:
a. The amount of the towing and storage charges to be assessed against the impounded vehicle; and
b. The extent of the liability of the owner for payment of the towing and storage charges so established.
(Ord. No. O-91-02, § 14-153, 3-4-91; Ord. No. O-22-11, § 2(Exh. A), 10-17-22)
805:

(a) Definitions. As used in this article, the following terms shall have the following meanings:
(1) Bicycle lane: A portion of the roadway that has been designated by striping, pavement markings, or signage for the exclusive or preferential use of persons operating bicycles, electric-assisted bicycles or motorized mobility devices.
(2) Bicycle path: A right-of-way under the jurisdiction and control of this state or a local political subdivision thereof designated for use by bicycle, electric-assisted bicycle and motorized mobility device operators. This includes a shared use path.
(3) Company: Any shared motorized mobility device vendor that has been issued a shared motorized mobility device permit by the city.
(4) Landscape zone: A buffer between the sidewalk and the curb line, which may include a combination of street furniture, lighting, and natural landscape elements.
(5) Motorized mobility device: A vehicle with a total weight of less than 75 pounds, equipped with or without handlebars, a floorboard for standing while operating, and two or three wheels; designed to transport only one individual; and manufactured with a power source capable of propelling the vehicle, unassisted on a paved level surface at a speed not to exceed 15 miles per hour, including, but not limited to, any such device owned and operated individually or operated through an agreement with a company.
(6) Operator: Any individual operating and/or in possession of a motorized mobility device.
(7) Shared motorized mobility device: A motorized mobility device made available for rent to the public, usually through a user agreement.
(8) Sidewalk: A portion of a street between the curb lines, or the lateral lines of a railway, and the adjacent property lines, intended for use by pedestrians.
